title: What people frame, viii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Friday, the last: a man buys a frame with nothing to put in it. 8×10. 'I'll know when I see it.' Wood sells it. The arc ends on an empty frame.

panels.composition: The counter. A MAN, sixties, plain. No bag, no envelope, nothing.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a plain man in his sixties at a frame-shop counter with empty hands asking for a frame, a young clerk, a dog

panels.composition: Wood setting the empty frame on the counter. Glass. Backing. Nothing between.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, close-up of an empty black eight-by-ten frame with glass and backing and nothing between them on a counter

panels.composition: The man looking through it at the shop. At Wood. At the dog.

balloons.text: I'll know when I see it.
Most people bring the thing first.
Most people already had the thing.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a man holding an empty frame up and looking through it at a young clerk and a dog

panels.composition: The man going out with the empty frame under his arm. Wood. The dog. The Owner. The shop. Twenty-five days of what people frame, ending on nothing in it.
panels.caption: Friday.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a man walking out of a frame shop with an empty frame under his arm, a young clerk, a dog and an older woman watching him go, no words

notes: 'Most people already had the thing.' The arc ends on an empty frame. Arc 1's aesthetic bleeds out here.
